best_for: Developers who work in Git all day and want a fast desktop client for staging single lines, reading diffs and resolving merges, and who will pay once for a license.

points.title: Try free, pay to keep using it
points.text: You can download and evaluate it for free, but continued use needs a license. A personal license is USD 99 with 3 years of updates. Business is USD 75 per user per year. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Stage exactly what you mean
points.text: You can stage whole files, hunks or single lines, and split a hunk by selecting lines. Diffs show side by side with syntax and character-level highlighting.

points.title: It shows the Git it runs
points.text: Sublime Merge works on top of Git and lets you see the exact Git commands behind each action, so what you learn carries over to the terminal.

points.title: Search, blame and merge in one place
points.text: Search runs as you type across commit messages, authors, paths and file contents. It also has a built-in merge tool, blame and file history, submodule handling and Git Flow support.

points.title: 64-bit only
points.text: Builds exist only for 64-bit systems. Windows gets an x64 installer for all users, plus a portable version on the official site. Mac gets one universal build.

points.title: Linux: site packages or Flatpak
points.text: Sublime HQ offers package repositories plus .deb, .rpm and tarball downloads for x64 and ARM64. The Flatpak listed here names Sublime HQ as developer, but Flathub does not mark it as verified. The Windows listing keeps 25 builds; macOS and Linux list only the current one.
